newsitem.title: USA: Four sentenced for fund-rasing at U.S. Ag Dep't.
newsitem.headline: Four sentenced for fund-rasing at U.S. Ag Dep't.

text.p: Four men involved in illegal political fund-raising at the Agriculture Department were sentenced Friday to two years' probation and ordered to pay modest fines.

U.S. Magistrate Patrick Attridge also ordered two of the men, Jack L. Webb and Jeffress A Wells, to serve 30 days in a halfway house. Webb and Wells allegedly prepared lists, at the request of a superior, of whom to reward and whom to punish at the department after President Clinton's election in 1992.
Prosecutor Laura Ingersoll declined to say if the Justice Department was still investigating the matter.
"I cannot address that," she told reporters.

Webb, Wells and codefendants Jack S. Folines and Grady Bilberry pleaded guilty in September to violating federal laws against politicking on the job. The men were supervisors in 1992 and solicited donations from underlings with the promise it would aid their careers if Clinton won.
Court documents said the fundraising was coordinated with an outsider who later was appointed to a senior post at the Agriculture Department.

An investigation by a House Agriculture subcommittee identified that person as Farm Service Agency chief Grant Buntrock, who has said he did nothing improper and that political affiliation played no role in job assignments.
During a subcommittee hearing, Ron Blackley, chief of staff to former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy, denied asking for lists of employees to be aided or squelched.
A report by the subcommittee said people who contributed money were rewarded while suspected Republican supporters were punished.
Attridge ordered Webb and Wells to pay a $2,500 fine and to perform 120 hours of community service, in addition to probation and time in a halfway house.
Forlines and Bilberry were ordered to pay fines of $1,000 and to perform 100 hours of community service, in addition to probation.
All four men apologized during sentencing for their actions." Webb, Wells and Forlines have retired from federal work.
"As a child, I was taught my sins would be found out and punished...Mine have. I trust you will have mercy," Forlines said to Attridge.
